Rough
rŭf
adj. (uneven, harsh, hairy, violent; rendering Hebrew rekes, eythan, sa'ar, and qashah, Greek trachus)
Old English rūh, hairy, shaggy; the sense of unevenness came from the feel of hair under the hand. The AV's rough garment is literally a hairy one.

Biblical Definition

Isaiah's highway for God: “the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain” (Isa 40:4), which the Baptist fulfilled — “the rough ways shall be made smooth” (Luk 3:5). In Daniel's vision “the rough goat is the king of Grecia” (Dan 8:21). Zechariah's false prophets shall no longer “wear a rough garment to deceive” (Zec 13:4). The heifer for an unsolved murder is brought “unto a rough valley, which is neither eared nor sown” (Deu 21:4). And of God's measured chastening: “he stayeth his rough wind in the day of the east wind” (Isa 27:8).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines rough as having inequalities on the surface; not smooth; harsh; severe; coarse; tempestuous; hairy, shaggy.

expand to see more

ROUGH, a. Having inequalities, small ridges or points on the surface; not smooth or plane; as a rough board; a rough stone.

2. Stormy; boisterous; tempestuous; as rough weather.

3. Harsh; severe; uncivil; rude; as a rough temper.

4. Hairy; shaggy; as a rough garment.

Key Scripture

Isa 40:4 — "Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low: and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain:"

Luk 3:5 — "Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough ways shall be made smooth;"

Dan 8:21 — "And the rough goat is the king of Grecia: and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king."

Zec 13:4 — "And it shall come to pass in that day, that the prophets shall be ashamed every one of his vision, when he hath prophesied; neither shall they wear a rough garment to deceive:"

Deu 21:4 — "And the elders of that city shall bring down the heifer unto a rough valley, which is neither eared nor sown, and shall strike off the heifer's neck there in the valley:"

Isa 27:8 — "In measure, when it shooteth forth, thou wilt debate with it: he stayeth his rough wind in the day of the east wind."

Modern Corruption

The rough garment is worn to look like a prophet, and Zechariah says the day is coming when no one will dare put it on.

expand to see more

Elijah wore hair and John wore camel's hair, and by Zechariah's day the costume had become the credential: a rough garment to deceive. The hair shirt, the studied severity, the rasp in the voice — every generation has men who put on the prophet's coat because it is easier than carrying the prophet's word, and Zechariah 13 foresees a day when the false prophets will be ashamed of their visions and disown the garment. Roughness is not holiness. Isaiah 40:4 uses the word the other way, for the ground the King will travel: the rough places plain, the crooked straight — the levelling that John preached as repentance, so that when the Lord came there would be no ridge of pride or pit of sin in the road. The roughness God wants removed is in the heart, and the roughness men put on is on the back.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew rekes (H7406), rough, rugged ground; eythan (H386), perennial, ever-flowing, rough; sa'ar (H8181), hair, hairy; sa'ir (H8163), a he-goat, shaggy; qashah (H7186), hard, rough; Greek trachus (G5138), rough.

expand to see more

Hebrew rekes (H7406) — rough, rugged; Isaiah 40:4 only; qashah (H7186), Isaiah 27:8.

Hebrew sa'ar (H8181) — hair, a hairy mantle; Zechariah 13:4, Genesis 25:25; sa'ir (H8163), the rough goat; Daniel 8:21; eythan (H386), Deuteronomy 21:4.

Greek trachus (G5138) — rough, rocky; Luke 3:5, Acts 27:29.

Usage

"“The rough places plain” — the road levelled for the King."

"“Wear a rough garment to deceive” — the costume as credential."

"“The rough goat is the king of Grecia” — prophecy's precision."
